# gh-1596: [GOAL] POSIX-sh portable first-run wizard — setup.sh completes under curl | sh on dash/busybox/bash (fixes #1596 crash)

## Description

## Goal — POSIX-sh portable first-run wizard (v1, converted from bug report)
One sentence: **`curl -fsSL https://fa1.dev/setup.sh | sh` completes the full first-run wizard and writes a working `~/.fah/config.yaml` under every mainstream POSIX sh — dash, busybox ash, bash — not only bash.**

Today `site/setup.sh` is bash-only: 7 uses of the bash builtin `printf -v`. Under `curl | sh` the shebang is ignored — whatever `sh` resolves to executes the script — and on Ubuntu 24.04 (sh = dash) the wizard aborts at the first prompt: `printf: Illegal option -v`. `.fah` is never created. Reported by an external user (khoser); this is the first-run experience for every new Linux user.

## Why this framing
- The fix lands in the **generator pipeline**, not the artifact: `site/install-config.yaml` + `site/setup.sh.template` → `scripts/gen_installers.dart` → `site/setup.sh` (`DO NOT EDIT BY HAND` header). A hand-patch of `site/setup.sh` regresses on the next release.
- Retracted framing: "add/fix the bash shebang" — under `curl | sh` a shebang is dead text; the script must be valid for whatever shell the pipe feeds. Never revisit.
- The wizard's interactive-stdin design is already correct (`read … < /dev/tty`, non-TTY guard at the top) — this card changes **nothing** about the UX, only the shell dialect.

## Architecture
```
site/install-config.yaml ─┐
site/setup.sh.template ───┴─> scripts/gen_installers.dart ──> site/setup.sh  (curl | sh target)
                                                            └> site/install.sh, install.bat/ps1
```
Invariants:
- **I1 (dialect):** every `sh`-targeted emitted script parses and runs under dash, busybox ash, and bash. POSIX subset only: no `printf -v`, no `[[ ]]`, no arrays, no `local -a`, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no `${var,,}`, no `=~`.
- **I2 (single source):** emitted `site/setup.sh` is byte-identical to a fresh regeneration (existing pin/selftest guards keep enforcing this).
- **I3 (UX parity):** prompt texts, provider menu, hidden key entry (`read -rs < /dev/tty`), and the non-TTY degradation path behave identically on bash and dash.

## Capability surface (what the wizard must do → portability shape)
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prompt helpers (`ask`, `ask_hidden`, `confirm`) | `printf -v` assignment (bash-only) | POSIX assignment via command substitution (`var=$(…)`) with exit-code propagation |
| Interactive stdin | `read -r < /dev/tty` (correct) | unchanged |
| Non-TTY path | guard at line 143, clear message | unchanged + IT-covered |
| Config write | `~/.fah/config.yaml` | unchanged (E3 pins no-clobber) |
| CI portability guard | none | **core**: dash + busybox smoke jobs |
| `shellcheck --shell=sh` over emitted sh | none | second tier (opt-in follow-up) |
| Non-interactive env setup (`FA_SETUP_PROVIDER=…`) | none | second tier (opt-in follow-up) |
| Rewrite wizard in another language / compiled helper | — | **excluded**: 400 lines of POSIX sh is the right tool; a binary bootstrap adds supply-chain surface for zero UX gain |
| Re-exec into bash from the piped script | — | **excluded**: impossible without writing a temp file from remote code — new attack surface; removing bashisms is strictly simpler |

### Platform facts (pinned, each with a test)
- **dash** (Ubuntu `sh`, Debian): `printf` has no `-v` → the #1596 crash. Negative test: dash run of the old script fails at line 74; positive: new script completes.
- **busybox ash** (Alpine, slim containers): same; also strict about `local` outside functions. Smoke-covered.
- **macOS `sh`** = bash 3.2 POSIX mode: *accepts* `printf -v` (bash builtin quirk) — that's why the bug never fired on macOS. Positive test only (no macOS regression possible from this fix).
- **`/dev/tty`** exists in interactive sessions, absent in non-interactive CI pipes → the existing non-TTY guard is the degradation path (IT-asserted).

### Security (remote `curl | sh` + typed secrets)
- Threat: the wizard collects a **provider API key**. Invariants: the key is read via `read -rs < /dev/tty` (never echoed), lands **only** in `~/.fah/config.yaml`, never appears in argv/`ps` output, transcripts, or logs; the config write keeps current file-mode behavior.
- The POSIX rewrite must not "simplify" hidden input into visible echo or pass the key through `printf` argv in a way `ps` can catch (assign via `read`, not `var=$(… key on the command line)`).
- Supply chain: served over HTTPS from fa1.dev; existing `check_install_pin.sh` / `installer_verify_selftest.sh` guards stay. Checksum infrastructure = separate card (out of scope).

## Freshness audit (fresh main `92e939246`, 2026-10-14)
The dialect bug is not the only problem — the wizard's data is stale. Verified against fresh main; all `site/` files are byte-identical to the generator output (no artifact drift), so every finding below lives in the **source** (`site/install-config.yaml` + template) and ships on every fresh download:

| Surface | Wizard offers | fa reality (origin/main) | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Providers | 5: openrouter, anthropic, google, openai, custom | **12** in `provider_catalog.dart`: + copilot, zai, kimi, codemie, dial, minimax, chatgpt, aiin | **stale** |
| Approval modes | 3: yolo, write, always-ask | **4**: + `autopilot` (`kAutopilotLabel`, formerly `unattended`) | **stale** |
| Model presets | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4 (recommended)`, `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, `claude-sonnet-4-5` | current catalog defaults | **stale** |
| Agent modes | code, architect, review | `builtInAgentModes` = default(code), architect, review | ✓ current |
| Config keys written | provider/model/baseUrl/mode/approvalMode/allowedTools | all live in `settings_registry` (`yamlKeys`) | ✓ current |
| Interactive stdin (`read < /dev/tty`), non-TTY guard | as designed | unchanged on main | ✓ current |

Provider surface is actively moving upstream (gh-1554 scoped timeouts, gh-1570 ProviderModelBinding) — another reason the wizard's provider data must be **generated from the live catalog**, not hand-maintained in yaml.

### Addition to the fix (same card)
- **AC6** — the wizard's provider list, approval-mode list, and model presets are **generated from `provider_catalog.dart`** (gen_installers reads the catalog or a checked-in snapshot with a drift test): provider menu names == catalog names, approval menu = always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot, presets = current recommended defaults. A catalog change without regeneration fails `UT-2` (golden drift, extended to the data sections).
- Provider menu ordering: keep openrouter first (recommended), then the rest by catalog order; `custom` stays last.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — `site/setup.sh.template` contains zero POSIX-violating constructs (automated scan: `printf -v`, `[[`, `read -p`, arrays, `${var,,}`, `=~`); regenerated `site/setup.sh` identical to the scan-clean template. Hook: `gen_installers` golden test + a new template lint.

- **AC3** — The hidden API key never appears in the captured transcript of the IT runs (byte-scan the fixture for the key literal) and `~/.fah/config.yaml` contains it exactly once.
- **AC4** — Non-TTY run prints the existing clear guidance and exits non-zero without writing `.fah` (parity with today's guard).
- **AC5** — `bash site/setup.sh` (direct, non-piped) behavior is unchanged (existing UX preserved; no prompt-text drift).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

- `flutter_app/lib/services/vision_models.dart` — shim re-exporting the
  `modelIdSuggestsVision` heuristic (fa_ui shim → the pure-Dart core
  `lib/src/model_roles/vision_models.dart`), which fills `Model.input`;
  `AgentConfig.supportsImages` overrides;
  without `image` the `read` tool notes non-vision and adapters drop image
  blocks.
- `flutter_app/lib/services/media_tools.dart` — `MediaGateway` over the
  `media_models.json` slots (+ main-connection fallback) backing the
  `generate_image`/`speak`/`generate_music`/`generate_video` tools and the
  `jsr.fa.media.*` bridge; files land in `generated/`. `generate_video`
  rides the `videoGeneration` slot (required — no fallback): async
  OpenAI/OpenRouter `/videos` contract (POST job → poll `GET /videos/{id}`
  every 3s, 4-min cap, cancel-token aware → `unsigned_urls` or
  `GET /videos/{id}/content` mp4). Google (`generativelanguage`) endpoints
  switch to the native Gemini protocol by baseUrl: `speak` posts
  `/models/{model}:generateContent` (`x-goog-api-key` auth, LINEAR16 PCM
  24 kHz mono wrapped into a `.wav`), `generate_music` posts
  `/interactions` with `{model, input}` and deep-searches the response for
  base64 audio; the image/video slots answer an honest "not supported for
  the Google provider yet" error.
- `docs/subagents/` — the subagents-2.0 + long-term-memory master plan
  (phased: memory package publish, memory foundation, memory-aware
  compaction, session-backed retained subagents, agent-type menu); update
  the checklists there as work lands.
- `site/` — static GitHub Pages landing; `.github/workflows/pages.yml`
  builds the web demo into `app/` (never committed). `site/privacy.html`
  is the published privacy policy (`PRIVACY.md` in the repo root is the
  source text — keep both in sync; the onboarding privacy page links to
  `https://fa1.dev/privacy.html`).
- `scripts/` — codegen and quality-gate scripts.
- `browser_ext/` — Chrome MV3 extension pairing fa with the browser
  (issue #23): `sw/main.js` (entry, pairing storage, panel API,
  optional embedded-agent boot), `sw/bridge.js` (wire protocol v1
  client), `sw/ops.js` (browserReq op table), `sw/tabs.js` (task tab
  groups), `sw/cdp.js` (chrome.debugger trusted path), `sw/agent.js`
  (dart2js build artifact, gitignored, absent → bridge-only scaffold),
  `content/content.js` (isolated-world DOM ops), `panel/` (side panel).
  `dart/` is the `fa_browser_agent` package (path dep) compiled into
  `sw/agent.js` by `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` — agent host,
  chrome.storage ExecutionEnv, provider streams (incl. deterministic
  `fake:` provider), DAP hub client. Tests: `browser_ext/dart/test`,
  `browser_ext/test` (node --test), `test/browser_ext/` (headless
  Chrome, integration tag). Docs: docs/browser-extension.md.
- `lib/src/browser/` — pure-Dart browser half: `bridge_protocol.dart`
  (wire protocol v1 — frame codec, ops/error codes, one-time
  `pairingToken()`, `browser-ext/` mailbox ids, reconnect backoff, mail
  dedupe) and `browser_tools.dart` (the eleven exec-tier `browser_*`
  tools over the injectable `BrowserController`; failures throw
  `BrowserToolException` carrying the wire code). Availability family
  `browser` + `browser_eval` in `agent_cli_tools.dart`
  (docs/tool-availability.md); CLI surface in
  `lib/src/cli/browser_bridge_commands.dart` (`/browser connect|status`).
- `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — `fa serve --bridge [--port N] [--token T]`
  loopback WebSocket bridge (binds 127.0.0.1 only, AC15; non-
  `chrome-extension://` origins refused): one-time token pairing
  (`.fah/bridge/token`, 0600, minted fresh per `/browser connect`),
  two-way mail relay over the messaging fabric, ping/pong keepalive,
  `browserReq`/`browserRes` correlation for the `browser_*` tools. The
  CLI mounts the same server in-process via `bin/fah.dart`'s
  `_FaBrowserBridgeHandle` (also the `BrowserController` seam).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved

+# gh-1596: this script runs under `curl | sh` — the shebang is dead text and
+# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +
+# bash): no `printf -v`, no `[[`, no arrays, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no
+# `${var,,}`, no `=~`. UT-1 (test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart) lints
+# the dialect; UT-2 pins the regenerated bytes.
+
 set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it
 
+# E4: an unset HOME would die later inside the config path with a bare
+# "parameter not set" — fail here, clearly, before anything else runs.
+if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
+  printf '\033[1;31m✘\033[0m %s\n' '$HOME is not set — cannot write the Fa config. Set HOME and re-run.' >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
 FAH_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.fah"
 FAH_CONFIG_FILE="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/config.yaml"
+FAH_TMP_CONF=""  # config write is atomic (tmp + mv); cleaned on any exit
+FAH_STTY_SAVED=""  # termios during hidden reads; restored on any exit
+
+trap 'rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"
+  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
+    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
+  fi' EXIT
 
 # ── TTY handling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 if [ -t 0 ]; then
@@ -47,48 +67,62 @@ err() {
 }
 
 # ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
+# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so

Key observations so far on the template:

1. `ask()` returns 1 on EOF, printing `$default`. But when read fails (EOF), `printf '%s' "$default"` — if default is empty, prints empty. And return 1 → under `set -eu`, the caller does `var=$(ask ...)` — assignment with command substitution: the exit status of the assignment is the exit status of the command substitution, so with `set -e` it aborts. Good.

Wait, there's a subtlety: `var=$(ask_yn ...)` — if ask_yn returns non-zero, `set -e` triggers, script exits non-zero. That's the designed "EOF aborts" behavior. But there's the reconfigure prompt: `reconfigure=$(ask_yn "..." "n")` — if user hits EOF at the reconfigure prompt, script aborts with non-zero and the EXIT trap cleans up. OK by design (E1).

2. `ask_hidden` uses `stty -g < /dev/tty`. Note: under dash, `stty -g` works. But what if `/dev/tty` exists but stty is missing? Edge case.

A subtle bug: in `ask_hidden`, `FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)` — under `set -eu`... wait, in `$(...)` with `|| true` — fine.

3. `read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty` — read by name. In dash, `read -r var` works. If read fails (EOF), variable is set to empty. Then returns 1 → set -e aborts. OK.

Hmm — but wait: in `ask_hidden`, after read, the value stays in the variable named by `$1`. Good, key never on argv.

But then how is the key written to the rc file? `sed -i.bak "s|^export ${key_var}=.*|export ${key_var}='${api_key}'|"` — the api_key is interpolated into the sed replacement. If the key contains `|` or `&` or backslashes, the sed breaks — E3 says values with spaces/quotes/`$`/trailing `/` stored verbatim, but this sed path is only for the shell rc persistence, pre-existing behavior? Let me check what main had. This line is in context (not changed in the diff). Actually the diff shows context around it but the sed line itself is unchanged (context line). Let me verify in the template.

4. The config write: `mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"` — atomic write. Good. But E2 (no-clobber) handled by the earlier reconfigure prompt.

Hmm — one issue: `FAH_TMP_CONF="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.tmp"` — a predictable temp file name in ~/.fah. Symlink attack: if an attacker pre-creates ~/.fah/.config.yaml.tmp as a symlink... but ~/.fah is the user's own dir; the tmp file is created by `>` redirection which follows symlinks. Local attack surface — low risk but the ticket is about a first-run wizard writing secrets. The final config write uses `sed -i` for rc too. Probably a SUGGESTION-level note (mktemp or checking -L). Actually the wizard runs as the user; an attacker with write access to ~/.fah could already clobber the config directly. So negligible.

5. Non-TTY path now exits 1 (was exit 0). AC4 requires non-zero. Good.

But wait — subtle: `[ ! -e /dev/tty ] || [ ! -t 2 ]` — under `set -u`, fine. curl | sh with a terminal but stdin is the pipe: /dev/tty exists, stderr is tty → proceeds to interactive. Good.

6. The EXIT trap: `trap 'rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"; if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null; fi' EXIT`. Note single quotes — evaluated at exit. Under `set -u`, `$FAH_TMP_CONF` is initialized to "" at the top. Good. But `stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty` — in a non-interactive context FAH_STTY_SAVED is empty → skipped. OK.

One question: `trap ... EXIT` on EXIT — when the non-TTY path exits 1, trap runs, rm -f "" → `rm -f` with empty arg → rm -f "" is fine (no error with -f). Actually `rm -f ""` — POSIX says rm -f with a nonexistent/empty operand exits 0 silently? `rm -f ""` prints an error in some shells? Let me test: `sh -c 'set -eu; T=""; trap "rm -f \$T" EXIT; exit 1'` — rm -f '' — GNU rm: "rm: cannot remove '': No such file or directory" — with -f, nonexistent files are ignored silently, but an EMPTY operand? Let me check. GNU rm -f "": rm: cannot remove '': No such file or directory? Actually with -f, "do not prompt... ignore nonexistent... never prompt". For empty string operand, coreutils treats it as ENOENT and -f suppresses the diagnostic. I believe `rm -f ''` is silent with exit 0 in GNU coreutils. Busybox too. Fine.

7. `ask()` no longer loops (`while true` dropped) — the old loop was pointless anyway. OK.

8. The old `ask` had `printf -v "$var" '%s' "$default"` on read failure + return 1. New one prints default + return 1. Under set -e the return 1 propagates through `var=$(ask ...)`.

Wait — actually there's a subtlety with `set -e` and command substitution in assignments: `var=$(false)` → assignment gets exit status 1 → set -e triggers. Yes.

But what about `value=$(ask "text")` where ask's `read` fails? Exit 1 propagates. Good — documented as intended EOF abort.

9. Provider/model/approval cases come from generator placeholders `{{APPROVAL_CASES}}` etc. Need to check gen_installers.dart.

10. Hidden key: `stty -echo < /dev/tty` then `read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY"`. FAH_TTY is presumably /dev/tty. In the IT they feed scripted input via pty.

One concern: `read -r "$1"` — if the provider key contains backslashes, read -r keeps them raw. Good.

Another concern: `ask_hidden` restores stty after EACH hidden read (and clears FAH_STTY_SAVED). The EXIT trap re-checks FAH_STTY_SAVED — fine.

11. What about `read` with IFS? Default IFS splits on whitespace — a key with spaces would only partially land in `$1`! `read -r "$1"` with input "abc def" → $1="abc", rest goes... with a single variable, the rest of the line including whitespace is assigned to that variable (read assigns the entire remainder to the last variable). Yes — with ONE variable, read -r assigns the whole line (minus trailing IFS whitespace? hmm). POSIX: "If there are fewer vars than fields, the last var gets the remaining fields INCLUDING the intervening IFS whitespace." So trailing whitespace is stripped? read strips trailing IFS whitespace from the line? For `read -r var`, leading/trailing IFS whitespace is trimmed. A key with trailing spaces — negligible. Key with internal spaces preserved. Fine.

12. Now the BIG question — the model selection and other `$(ask ...)` uses: `var=$(ask ...)` runs `ask` in a SUBSHELL. The prompt writes to /dev/tty, reads from $FAH_TTY. Fine.

But `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME precisely because it must run in the parent shell (subshell would lose the var) — that's why its API differs from ask/ask_yn. Consistent.

13. Stty saved state: `FAH_STTY_SAVED` assignment inside `ask_hidden`... `ask_hidden` is called as a plain function (not in subshell), so FAH_STTY_SAVED persists. Good.

14. Also `set -eu`: in ask_hidden, `local read_ok=0`, `if read...; then read_ok=1; fi`. If read fails, `if` guards it. OK. But what about `[ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0` then `return 1` — fine.

Wait — one more: in `ask`, `if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then printf '%s' "$default"; return 1; fi` — under set -e, `read` in an `if` condition is exempt. Good.

15. Now — `local` keyword: dash supports `local` inside functions (dash does support local). Busybox ash too. Fine.

16. Check `set -eu` comment: "no pipefail: dash lacks it" — fine.

17. HOME check: good (E4).

18. `printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty` — prompt writes to tty. In a `$(...)` subshell, stdout captured, so writing prompts to tty is required. OK.

Now, potential ISSUE: the EXIT trap is single-quoted and references `$FAH_TMP_CONF` and `$FAH_STTY_SAVED` at exit time — good design. But `stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED"` — the saved string is like "gdoch1: \..." — passing as ONE arg to stty. Correct usage.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — interactive configuration wizard for the Fa CLI.
#              Run this after `install.sh` to pick a provider, model, API key,
#              mode and approval policy.
#
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh
#
# What it does:
#   1. Verifies `fa` is installed.
#   2. Interactively picks a provider + model (or a custom endpoint).
#   3. Collects the API key and writes ~/.fah/config.yaml.
#   4. Optionally persists the API key in your shell startup file.
#
# {{GENERATED_HEADER}}

# gh-1596: this script runs under `curl | sh` — the shebang is dead text and
# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +
# bash): no `printf -v`, no `[[`, no arrays, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no
# `${var,,}`, no `=~`. UT-1 (test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart) lints
# the dialect; UT-2 pins the regenerated bytes.

set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it

# E4: an unset HOME would die later inside the config path with a bare
# "parameter not set" — fail here, clearly, before anything else runs.
if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
  printf '\033[1;31m✘\033[0m %s\n' '$HOME is not set — cannot write the Fa config. Set HOME and re-run.' >&2
  exit 1
fi

FAH_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.fah"
FAH_CONFIG_FILE="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/config.yaml"
FAH_TMP_CONF=""  # config write is atomic (tmp + mv); cleaned on any exit
FAH_STTY_SAVED=""  # termios during hidden reads; restored on any exit

trap 'rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi' EXIT

# ── TTY handling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  FAH_TTY="/dev/stdin"
else
  FAH_TTY="/dev/tty"
fi

# ── Output helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
say() {
  printf '%s\n' "$*"
}

info() {
  printf '\033[1;34m→\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

ok() {
  printf '\033[1;32m✔\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

warn() {
  printf '\033[1;33m!\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2
}

err() {
  printf '\033[1;31m✘\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2
}

# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

# ── Banner ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
say ""
say "  ███████╗ █████╗       ████████╗███████╗██████╗ ███╗   ███╗██╗███╗   ██╗ █████╗ ██╗"
say "  ██╔════╝██╔══██╗      ╚══██╔══╝██╔════╝██╔══██╗████╗ ████║██║████╗  ██║██╔══██╗██║"
say "  █████╗  ███████║█████╗   ██║   █████╗  ██████╔╝██╔████╔██║██║██╔██╗ ██║███████║██║"
say "  ██╔══╝  ██╔══██║╚════╝   ██║   ██╔══╝  ██╔══██╗██║╚██╔╝██║██║██║╚██╗██║██╔══██║██║"
say "  ██║     ██║  ██║         ██║   ███████╗██║  ██║██║ ╚═╝ ██║██║██║ ╚████║██║  ██║███████╗"
say "  ╚═╝     ╚═╝  ╚═╝         ╚═╝   ╚══════╝╚═╝  ╚═╝╚═╝     ╚═╝╚═╝╚═╝  ╚═══╝╚═╝  ╚═╝╚══════╝"
say ""
say "  Fa setup wizard — flutter_agent_harness CLI"
say ""

# ── 1. Verify CLI is installed ───────────────────────────────────────────────
if ! command -v fa >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! command -v fah >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  err "'fa' is not on your PATH."
  say ""
  say "  Run the installer first:"
  say ""
  say "    curl -fsSL \"https://fa1.dev/install.sh\" | sh"
  say ""
  say "  Then reload your shell (or open a new terminal) and run this wizard again:"
  say ""
  say "    curl -fsSL \"https://fa1.dev/setup.sh\" | sh"
  say ""
  exit 1
fi
ok "Found 'fa' on PATH ($(command -v fa 2>/dev/null || command -v fah))."

# ── 2. Interactive configuration ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# AC4 (gh-1596): a non-TTY run (piped CI, curl|sh without a terminal) cannot
# collect answers — print the guidance and exit NON-ZERO so callers never
# read the run as a completed setup.
if [ ! -e /dev/tty ] || [ ! -t 2 ]; then
  info "Non-interactive environment detected."
  say ""
  say "  To finish setup, set an API key and run:"
  say ""
  say "    fa"
  say ""
  exit 1
fi

if [ -f "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
  reconfigure=$(ask_yn "A config already exists at ${FAH_CONFIG_FILE}. Reconfigure?" "n")
  if [ "$reconfigure" != "y" ]; then
    ok "Kept existing config. Run 'fa' to start."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

say ""
info "Let's configure your default provider and model."
say ""

{{PROVIDER_MENU}}

{{PROVIDER_CASES}}

# API key
say ""
api_key=""
if [ "$provider" = "custom" ]; then
  needs_key=$(ask_yn "Does this endpoint require an API key?" "n")
  if [ "$needs_key" = "y" ]; then
    ask_hidden api_key "Paste your API key"
  fi

fi

{{MODE_MENU}}

{{MODE_CASES}}

{{APPROVAL_MENU}}

{{APPROVAL_CASES}}

# Write config.yaml — atomically (E1, gh-1596): the content is built in a
# temp file and renamed over the target, so a Ctrl-C mid-write can never
# leave a truncated config behind. printf-per-line keeps every value
# verbatim (E3: spaces, quotes, `$`, backticks, trailing slashes survive
# byte-for-byte — no heredoc expansion to trip over).
mkdir -p "$FAH_CONFIG_DIR"
FAH_TMP_CONF="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.tmp"
{
  printf 'provider: %s\n' "$provider_kind"

    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.

    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task

# gh-1596: [GOAL] POSIX-sh portable first-run wizard — setup.sh completes under curl | sh on dash/busybox/bash (fixes #1596 crash)

## Description

## Goal — POSIX-sh portable first-run wizard (v1, converted from bug report)
One sentence: **`curl -fsSL https://fa1.dev/setup.sh | sh` completes the full first-run wizard and writes a working `~/.fah/config.yaml` under every mainstream POSIX sh — dash, busybox ash, bash — not only bash.**

Today `site/setup.sh` is bash-only: 7 uses of the bash builtin `printf -v`. Under `curl | sh` the shebang is ignored — whatever `sh` resolves to executes the script — and on Ubuntu 24.04 (sh = dash) the wizard aborts at the first prompt: `printf: Illegal option -v`. `.fah` is never created. Reported by an external user (khoser); this is the first-run experience for every new Linux user.

## Why this framing
- The fix lands in the **generator pipeline**, not the artifact: `site/install-config.yaml` + `site/setup.sh.template` → `scripts/gen_installers.dart` → `site/setup.sh` (`DO NOT EDIT BY HAND` header). A hand-patch of `site/setup.sh` regresses on the next release.
- Retracted framing: "add/fix the bash shebang" — under `curl | sh` a shebang is dead text; the script must be valid for whatever shell the pipe feeds. Never revisit.
- The wizard's interactive-stdin design is already correct (`read … < /dev/tty`, non-TTY guard at the top) — this card changes **nothing** about the UX, only the shell dialect.

## Architecture
```
site/install-config.yaml ─┐
site/setup.sh.template ───┴─> scripts/gen_installers.dart ──> site/setup.sh  (curl | sh target)
                                                            └> site/install.sh, install.bat/ps1
```
Invariants:
- **I1 (dialect):** every `sh`-targeted emitted script parses and runs under dash, busybox ash, and bash. POSIX subset only: no `printf -v`, no `[[ ]]`, no arrays, no `local -a`, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no `${var,,}`, no `=~`.
- **I2 (single source):** emitted `site/setup.sh` is byte-identical to a fresh regeneration (existing pin/selftest guards keep enforcing this).
- **I3 (UX parity):** prompt texts, provider menu, hidden key entry (`read -rs < /dev/tty`), and the non-TTY degradation path behave identically on bash and dash.

## Capability surface (what the wizard must do → portability shape)
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prompt helpers (`ask`, `ask_hidden`, `confirm`) | `printf -v` assignment (bash-only) | POSIX assignment via command substitution (`var=$(…)`) with exit-code propagation |
| Interactive stdin | `read -r < /dev/tty` (correct) | unchanged |
| Non-TTY path | guard at line 143, clear message | unchanged + IT-covered |
| Config write | `~/.fah/config.yaml` | unchanged (E3 pins no-clobber) |
| CI portability guard | none | **core**: dash + busybox smoke jobs |
| `shellcheck --shell=sh` over emitted sh | none | second tier (opt-in follow-up) |
| Non-interactive env setup (`FA_SETUP_PROVIDER=…`) | none | second tier (opt-in follow-up) |
| Rewrite wizard in another language / compiled helper | — | **excluded**: 400 lines of POSIX sh is the right tool; a binary bootstrap adds supply-chain surface for zero UX gain |
| Re-exec into bash from the piped script | — | **excluded**: impossible without writing a temp file from remote code — new attack surface; removing bashisms is strictly simpler |

### Platform facts (pinned, each with a test)
- **dash** (Ubuntu `sh`, Debian): `printf` has no `-v` → the #1596 crash. Negative test: dash run of the old script fails at line 74; positive: new script completes.
- **busybox ash** (Alpine, slim containers): same; also strict about `local` outside functions. Smoke-covered.
- **macOS `sh`** = bash 3.2 POSIX mode: *accepts* `printf -v` (bash builtin quirk) — that's why the bug never fired on macOS. Positive test only (no macOS regression possible from this fix).
- **`/dev/tty`** exists in interactive sessions, absent in non-interactive CI pipes → the existing non-TTY guard is the degradation path (IT-asserted).

### Security (remote `curl | sh` + typed secrets)
- Threat: the wizard collects a **provider API key**. Invariants: the key is read via `read -rs < /dev/tty` (never echoed), lands **only** in `~/.fah/config.yaml`, never appears in argv/`ps` output, transcripts, or logs; the config write keeps current file-mode behavior.
- The POSIX rewrite must not "simplify" hidden input into visible echo or pass the key through `printf` argv in a way `ps` can catch (assign via `read`, not `var=$(… key on the command line)`).
- Supply chain: served over HTTPS from fa1.dev; existing `check_install_pin.sh` / `installer_verify_selftest.sh` guards stay. Checksum infrastructure = separate card (out of scope).

## Freshness audit (fresh main `92e939246`, 2026-10-14)
The dialect bug is not the only problem — the wizard's data is stale. Verified against fresh main; all `site/` files are byte-identical to the generator output (no artifact drift), so every finding below lives in the **source** (`site/install-config.yaml` + template) and ships on every fresh download:

| Surface | Wizard offers | fa reality (origin/main) | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Providers | 5: openrouter, anthropic, google, openai, custom | **12** in `provider_catalog.dart`: + copilot, zai, kimi, codemie, dial, minimax, chatgpt, aiin | **stale** |
| Approval modes | 3: yolo, write, always-ask | **4**: + `autopilot` (`kAutopilotLabel`, formerly `unattended`) | **stale** |
| Model presets | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4 (recommended)`, `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, `claude-sonnet-4-5` | current catalog defaults | **stale** |
| Agent modes | code, architect, review | `builtInAgentModes` = default(code), architect, review | ✓ current |
| Config keys written | provider/model/baseUrl/mode/approvalMode/allowedTools | all live in `settings_registry` (`yamlKeys`) | ✓ current |
| Interactive stdin (`read < /dev/tty`), non-TTY guard | as designed | unchanged on main | ✓ current |

Provider surface is actively moving upstream (gh-1554 scoped timeouts, gh-1570 ProviderModelBinding) — another reason the wizard's provider data must be **generated from the live catalog**, not hand-maintained in yaml.

### Addition to the fix (same card)
- **AC6** — the wizard's provider list, approval-mode list, and model presets are **generated from `provider_catalog.dart`** (gen_installers reads the catalog or a checked-in snapshot with a drift test): provider menu names == catalog names, approval menu = always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot, presets = current recommended defaults. A catalog change without regeneration fails `UT-2` (golden drift, extended to the data sections).
- Provider menu ordering: keep openrouter first (recommended), then the rest by catalog order; `custom` stays last.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — `site/setup.sh.template` contains zero POSIX-violating constructs (automated scan: `printf -v`, `[[`, `read -p`, arrays, `${var,,}`, `=~`); regenerated `site/setup.sh` identical to the scan-clean template. Hook: `gen_installers` golden test + a new template lint.
- **AC2** — Piped wizard (`curl -fsSL … | sh` equivalent: `dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'`) with scripted `/dev/tty` answers picks Custom (option 5), accepts endpoint+key, writes a valid `~/.fah/config.yaml`, exits 0 — under **dash**, **busybox ash**, and **bash**. Hook: IT pty harness.
- **AC3** — The hidden API key never appears in the captured transcript of the IT runs (byte-scan the fixture for the key literal) and `~/.fah/config.yaml` contains it exactly once.
- **AC4** — Non-TTY run prints the existing clear guidance and exits non-zero without writing `.fah` (parity with today's guard).
- **AC5** — `bash site/setup.sh` (direct, non-piped) behavior is unchanged (existing UX preserved; no prompt-text drift).

## Test plan
### Test matrix
- `UT-1` — template lint: forbidden-construct scan (AC1). Pure grep/dart, no IO.
- `UT-2` — golden drift: emitted `site/setup.sh` == regeneration from template+yaml (AC1; extends the existing selftest).
- `IT-1` — dash pty run, full wizard, option 5 Custom, fixture config asserted (AC2, AC3).
- `IT-2` — busybox ash pty run, same fixture (AC2).
- `IT-3`…

# Rework: validation CI red on head 80fbd94d — fixed

## Issues/Notes

Validation CI was red on 4 checks (`Core tests (shard 0/4)`, `Core tests (shard 2/4)`,
`Hostile ambient env`, `Quality gate`). The full logs reduce to exactly **two root
causes** — both pre-existing CI-wiring guards that the PR's new
`installer-portability` leg tripped; the leg itself and the wizard rewrite are
correct (all 26 UTs + all 13 dash/busybox/bash pty ITs pass on the PR head):

1. **`test/release_flow_race_test.dart` (shard 0 + hostile-env)** — the
   `#1368: quality-gate exports dart_ok; platform legs cannot redden it` test
   pins the gate's platform-exempt case pattern **verbatim**, ending
   `…|flutter-app-lock-smoke)`. The PR deliberately appended
   `|installer-portability` to that pattern in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
   (gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: a red dash/busybox/bash leg blocks the MERGE via the
   aggregate but never holds the pure-Dart publish hostage — same class as
   `installer-verify`). The stale pin no longer matched.

2. **`test/scripts/build_site_test.dart` (shard 2 + hostile-env)** — the
   gh-1476 guard forbids `dart test/site/` (dart exits 64 treating it as a
   command name) with a blunt `isNot(contains('dart test/site/'))` over the
   post-GEO region of `ci.yml`. The new leg's valid two-target invocation
   `run: dart test test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart
   test/site/installer_golden_test.dart` forms that exact char sequence
   **across the argument boundary** (`…a_test.dart␣test/site/…`) — a false
   positive, not the gh-1476 failure shape.

`Quality gate` failed only because its child legs (shards 0/2, hostile-env) were
red — no gate-side change needed. No open review threads on this PR.

## Approach

Kept the PR's intended `ci.yml` unchanged (the platform classification of
`installer-portability` is deliberate and documented in the PR, the workflow
comments, and the new `ci_1596_installer_portability_ci_test.dart`), and fixed
the two stale/blunt guards, RED→GREEN per TDD (both tests failed on the tree
before the fix, pass after; no production code touched):

- `release_flow_race_test.dart`: updated the verbatim pin to the new pattern
  tail `…|flutter-app-lock-smoke|installer-portability)` — now consistent with
  both the actual workflow and the PR's own classification test.
- `build_site_test.dart`: anchored the gh-1476 guard to **command position**
  (the bug shape that actually shipped): an inline `run: dart test/site/…` and
  a block-scalar line starting with `dart test/site/` stay forbidden, while a
  valid multi-target line (`…dart test test/site/a.dart test/site/b.dart`) is
  green. Added honest self-checks (#1100 pattern): both bad shapes must match,
  the legit multi-target shape must not — so the loosened guard cannot rot.

## Files Modified

- `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` — platform-exempt pattern pin now includes
  `installer-portability` (gh-1596 REG legs ride the #1368 publish-exempt class).
- `test/scripts/build_site_test.dart` — `dart test/site/` guard re-anchored to
  command position (inline + block-scalar), with self-check fixtures for both
  bug shapes and the multi-target argument boundary.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

  switch to the native Gemini protocol by baseUrl: `speak` posts
  `/models/{model}:generateContent` (`x-goog-api-key` auth, LINEAR16 PCM
  24 kHz mono wrapped into a `.wav`), `generate_music` posts
  `/interactions` with `{model, input}` and deep-searches the response for
  base64 audio; the image/video slots answer an honest "not supported for
  the Google provider yet" error.

  (phased: memory package publish, memory foundation, memory-aware
  compaction, session-backed retained subagents, agent-type menu); update
  the checklists there as work lands.
- `site/` — static GitHub Pages landing; `.github/workflows/pages.yml`
  builds the web demo into `app/` (never committed). `site/privacy.html`
  is the published privacy policy (`PRIVACY.md` in the repo root is the
  source text — keep both in sync; the onboarding privacy page links to
  `https://fa1.dev/privacy.html`).
- `scripts/` — codegen and quality-gate scripts.
- `browser_ext/` — Chrome MV3 extension pairing fa with the browser
  (issue #23): `sw/main.js` (entry, pairing storage, panel API,
  optional embedded-agent boot), `sw/bridge.js` (wire protocol v1
  client), `sw/ops.js` (browserReq op table), `sw/tabs.js` (task tab
  groups), `sw/cdp.js` (chrome.debugger trusted path), `sw/agent.js`
  (dart2js build artifact, gitignored, absent → bridge-only scaffold),
  `content/content.js` (isolated-world DOM ops), `panel/` (side panel).
  `dart/` is the `fa_browser_agent` package (path dep) compiled into
  `sw/agent.js` by `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` — agent host,
  chrome.storage ExecutionEnv, provider streams (incl. deterministic
  `fake:` provider), DAP hub client. Tests: `browser_ext/dart/test`,
  `browser_ext/test` (node --test), `test/browser_ext/` (headless
  Chrome, integration tag). Docs: docs/browser-extension.md.
- `lib/src/browser/` — pure-Dart browser half: `bridge_protocol.dart`
  (wire protocol v1 — frame codec, ops/error codes, one-time
  `pairingToken()`, `browser-ext/` mailbox ids, reconnect backoff, mail
  dedupe) and `browser_tools.dart` (the eleven exec-tier `browser_*`
  tools over the injectable `BrowserController`; failures throw
  `BrowserToolException` carrying the wire code). Availability family
  `browser` + `browser_eval` in `agent_cli_tools.dart`
  (docs/tool-availability.md); CLI surface in
  `lib/src/cli/browser_bridge_commands.dart` (`/browser connect|status`).
- `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — `fa serve --bridge [--port N] [--token T]`
  loopback WebSocket bridge (binds 127.0.0.1 only, AC15; non-
  `chrome-extension://` origins refused): one-time token pairing
  (`.fah/bridge/token`, 0600, minted fresh per `/browser connect`),
  two-way mail relay over the messaging fabric, ping/pong keepalive,
  `browserReq`/`browserRes` correlation for the `browser_*` tools. The
  CLI mounts the same server in-process via `bin/fah.dart`'s
  `_FaBrowserBridgeHandle` (also the `BrowserController` seam).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved

1. `ask()` returns 1 on EOF, printing `$default`. But when read fails (EOF), `printf '%s' "$default"` — if default is empty, prints empty. And return 1 → under `set -eu`, the caller does `var=$(ask ...)` — assignment with command substitution: the exit status of the assignment is the exit status of the command substitution, so with `set -e` it aborts. Good.

Wait, there's a subtlety: `var=$(ask_yn ...)` — if ask_yn returns non-zero, `set -e` triggers, script exits non-zero. That's the designed "EOF aborts" behavior. But there's the reconfigure prompt: `reconfigure=$(ask_yn "..." "n")` — if user hits EOF at the reconfigure prompt, script aborts with non-zero and the EXIT trap cleans up. OK by design (E1).

2. `ask_hidden` uses `stty -g < /dev/tty`. Note: under dash, `stty -g` works. But what if `/dev/tty` exists but stty is missing? Edge case.

A subtle bug: in `ask_hidden`, `FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)` — under `set -eu`... wait, in `$(...)` with `|| true` — fine.

3. `read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty` — read by name. In dash, `read -r var` works. If read fails (EOF), variable is set to empty. Then returns 1 → set -e aborts. OK.

Hmm — but wait: in `ask_hidden`, after read, the value stays in the variable named by `$1`. Good, key never on argv.

But then how is the key written to the rc file? `sed -i.bak "s|^export ${key_var}=.*|export ${key_var}='${api_key}'|"` — the api_key is interpolated into the sed replacement. If the key contains `|` or `&` or backslashes, the sed breaks — E3 says values with spaces/quotes/`$`/trailing `/` stored verbatim, but this sed path is only for the shell rc persistence, pre-existing behavior? Let me check what main had. This line is in context (not changed in the diff). Actually the diff shows context around it but the sed line itself is unchanged (context line). Let me verify in the template.

4. The config write: `mv -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF" "$FAH_CONFIG_FILE"` — atomic write. Good. But E2 (no-clobber) handled by the earlier reconfigure prompt.

Hmm — one issue: `FAH_TMP_CONF="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/.config.yaml.tmp"` — a predictable temp file name in ~/.fah. Symlink attack: if an attacker pre-creates ~/.fah/.config.yaml.tmp as a symlink... but ~/.fah is the user's own dir; the tmp file is created by `>` redirection which follows symlinks. Local attack surface — low risk but the ticket is about a first-run wizard writing secrets. The final config write uses `sed -i` for rc too. Probably a SUGGESTION-level note (mktemp or checking -L). Actually the wizard runs as the user; an attacker with write access to ~/.fah could already clobber the config directly. So negligible.

But wait — subtle: `[ ! -e /dev/tty ] || [ ! -t 2 ]` — under `set -u`, fine. curl | sh with a terminal but stdin is the pipe: /dev/tty exists, stderr is tty → proceeds to interactive. Good.

For empty string operand, coreutils treats it as ENOENT and -f suppresses the diagnostic. I believe `rm -f ''` is silent with exit 0 in GNU coreutils. Busybox too. Fine.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — interactive configuration wizard for the Fa CLI.
#              Run this after `install.sh` to pick a provider, model, API key,
#              mode and approval policy.
#
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh
#
# What it does:
#   1. Verifies `fa` is installed.
#   2. Interactively picks a provider + model (or a custom endpoint).
#   3. Collects the API key and writes ~/.fah/config.yaml.
#   4. Optionally persists the API key in your shell startup file.
#
# {{GENERATED_HEADER}}

# gh-1596: this script runs under `curl | sh` — the shebang is dead text and
# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +
# bash): no `printf -v`, no `[[`, no arrays, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no
# `${var,,}`, no `=~`. UT-1 (test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart) lints
# the dialect; UT-2 pins the regenerated bytes.

set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it

# E4: an unset HOME would die later inside the config path with a bare
# "parameter not set" — fail here, clearly, before anything else runs.
if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
  printf '\033[1;31m✘\033[0m %s\n' '$HOME is not set — cannot write the Fa config. Set HOME and re-run.' >&2
  exit 1
fi

FAH_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.fah"
FAH_CONFIG_FILE="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/config.yaml"
FAH_TMP_CONF=""  # config write is atomic (tmp + mv); cleaned on any exit
FAH_STTY_SAVED=""  # termios during hidden reads; restored on any exit

trap 'rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi' EXIT

# ── TTY handling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  FAH_TTY="/dev/stdin"
else
  FAH_TTY="/dev/tty"
fi

# ── Output helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
say() {
  printf '%s\n' "$*"
}

info() {
  printf '\033[1;34m→\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

ok() {
  printf '\033[1;32m✔\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

warn() {
  printf '\033[1;33m!\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2
}

err() {
  printf '\033[1;31m✘\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2
}

# ── Interactive helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# POSIX assignment discipline (gh-1596): `ask`/`ask_yn` print the answer on
# stdout and callers assign via command substitution — `var=$(ask …)` — so
# the exit code propagates (EOF under `set -eu` aborts the wizard, exactly
# like the old bare-call + `printf -v` shape). `ask_hidden` assigns BY NAME
# through `read -rs "$1"`: the API key moves from the tty straight into the
# variable and never passes through printf argv, where `ps` could catch it.
prompt() {
  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m ' "$1" > /dev/tty
}

ask() { # ask TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints the answer on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-}" value
  if [ -n "$default" ]; then
    prompt "$text [$default]"
  else
    prompt "$text"
  fi
  if ! read -r value < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    printf '%s' "$default"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$value" ] && [ -n "$default" ]; then
    value=$default
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$value"
  return 0
}

ask_hidden() { # ask_hidden VAR TEXT — reads hidden input into $VAR by name
  prompt "$2"
  # dash's read has NO -s (probed in the IT platform facts) — hide the
  # entry with stty on the controlling tty instead. `stty -g` snapshots
  # the full termios for a byte-exact restore (the EXIT trap re-runs it,
  # so even Ctrl-C mid-key re-enables echo). The value travels tty →
  # variable BY NAME and never rides printf argv, where ps could catch it.
  if [ -z "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=$(stty -g < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi
  stty -echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  local read_ok=0
  if read -r "$1" < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
    read_ok=1
  fi
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
    FAH_STTY_SAVED=""
  else
    stty echo < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi
  printf '\n' > /dev/tty
  [ "$read_ok" -eq 1 ] && return 0
  return 1
}

ask_yn() { # ask_yn TEXT [DEFAULT] — prints y or n on stdout
  local text="$1" default="${2:-y}" answer
  while true; do
    if [ "$default" = "y" ]; then
      prompt "$text [Y/n]"
    else
      prompt "$text [y/N]"
    fi
    if ! read -r answer < "$FAH_TTY" 2>/dev/tty; then
      printf '%s' "$default"
      return 1
    fi
    answer=${answer:-$default}
    case "$answer" in
      [Yy]|"" ) printf 'y\n'; return 0 ;;
      [Nn]    ) printf 'n\n'; return 0 ;;
    esac
    warn "please answer y or n"
  done
}

# ── Banner ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
say ""
say "  ███████╗ █████╗       ████████╗███████╗██████╗ ███╗   ███╗██╗███╗   ██╗ █████╗ ██╗"

say "  ██║     ██║  ██║         ██║   ███████╗██║  ██║██║ ╚═╝ ██║██║██║ ╚████║██║  ██║███████╗"
say "  ╚═╝     ╚═╝  ╚═╝         ╚═╝   ╚══════╝╚═╝  ╚═╝╚═╝     ╚═╝╚═╝╚═╝  ╚═══╝╚═╝  ╚═╝╚══════╝"
say ""
say "  Fa setup wizard — flutter_agent_harness CLI"
say ""

# ── 1. Verify CLI is installed ───────────────────────────────────────────────
if ! command -v fa >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! command -v fah >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  err "'fa' is not on your PATH."
  say ""
  say "  Run the installer first:"
  say ""
  say "    curl -fsSL \"https://fa1.dev/install.sh\" | sh"
  say ""
  say "  Then reload your shell (or open a new terminal) and run this wizard again:"
  say ""
  say "    curl -fsSL \"https://fa1.dev/setup.sh\" | sh"
  say ""

fi

# ── 2. Interactive configuration ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# AC4 (gh-1596): a non-TTY run (piped CI, curl|sh without a terminal) cannot

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# setup.sh — interactive configuration wizard for the Fa CLI.
#              Run this after `install.sh` to pick a provider, model, API key,
#              mode and approval policy.
#
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh
#
# What it does:
#   1. Verifies `fa` is installed.
#   2. Interactively picks a provider + model (or a custom endpoint).
#   3. Collects the API key and writes ~/.fah/config.yaml.
#   4. Optionally persists the API key in your shell startup file.
#
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE BY HAND. It is generated from site/install-config.yaml
#  by `dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart`.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# gh-1596: this script runs under `curl | sh` — the shebang is dead text and
# whatever `sh` resolves to executes it. POSIX sh only (dash + busybox ash +
# bash): no `printf -v`, no `[[`, no arrays, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no
# `${var,,}`, no `=~`. UT-1 (test/site/setup_sh_portability_test.dart) lints
# the dialect; UT-2 pins the regenerated bytes.

set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it

# E4: an unset HOME would die later inside the config path with a bare
# "parameter not set" — fail here, clearly, before anything else runs.
if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
  printf '\033[1;31m✘\033[0m %s\n' '$HOME is not set — cannot write the Fa config. Set HOME and re-run.' >&2
  exit 1
fi

FAH_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.fah"
FAH_CONFIG_FILE="$FAH_CONFIG_DIR/config.yaml"
FAH_TMP_CONF=""  # config write is atomic (tmp + mv); cleaned on any exit
FAH_STTY_SAVED=""  # termios during hidden reads; restored on any exit

trap 'rm -f "$FAH_TMP_CONF"
  if [ -n "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" ]; then
    stty "$FAH_STTY_SAVED" < /dev/tty 2>/dev/null
  fi' EXIT

# ── TTY handling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  FAH_TTY="/dev/stdin"
else
  FAH_TTY="/dev/tty"
fi

# ── Output helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
say() {
  printf '%s\n' "$*"
}

info() {
  printf '\033[1;34m→\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

ok() {
  printf '\033[1;32m✔\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

warn() {
